case_title: Jagjit Singh v. State of Punjab
accused_socioeconomic_status: Described as an average family, less well off than the victim's sister's family; the appellant contended he earned Rs.3000/- per month.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B (dowry death); Evidence Act s.113-B (presumption); IPC s.406 (accused acquitted at trial); IPC s.498-A (referred to, no separate conviction recorded)
evidence_type: Oral testimony (victim's father, elder sister, PCO operator, PCO witness); medical (post-mortem opinion on time of death); circumstantial (proximity of alleged cruelty to death)
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged beatings, taunting and expulsion from home over demand for a Maruti car or Rs.2 lakh; alleged beating the night before death, if believed
mitigating_circumstances: Appellant's father contributed to the victim's continued higher education; father acquitted at trial
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.304-B; sentenced to 8 years rigorous imprisonment; acquitted under s.406 IPC; no separate s.498-A conviction recorded
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction under s.304-B affirmed; sentence reduced from 8 years to 7 years RI
neutral_facts: The victim was married to the accused in January 1998 and died within about three years of the marriage, along with her young child, by drowning in a river. The prosecution case was that after the marriage the accused and other in-laws repeatedly beat and taunted the victim for bringing insufficient dowry and demanded a Maruti car or two lakh rupees. The victim's father testified that the victim told him about the maltreatment and that he gave the victim a fixed deposit receipt for thirty thousand rupees and spoke to the accused by phone. The victim's elder sister testified that on 16 February 2001 the victim visited her home, wept, complained of cruelty and said the accused had beaten her the previous night after she tried to stop him abusing her father; the victim's daughter was present. The same day the victim telephoned her father from a public call office, saying she had been maltreated, thrown out of the house, and would not be allowed back without a car or two lakh rupees. The operator at the call office and another witness saw the victim weeping during the call but could not hear the conversation. The post-mortem doctor estimated that about twelve days had elapsed between death and the post-mortem, placing the death on 16 or 17 February 2001. The victim's body and the child's body were found secured together with one chunni. The FIR was lodged on 17 February 2001.
physical_harm: Death of the victim and of her child by drowning in a river
number_of_offences: 3 charged (IPC s.304-B, s.406, s.498-A); 1 finally upheld (s.304-B)
motive: Alleged demand for dowry in the form of a Maruti car or Rs.2 lakh; the court treated this as cruelty in connection with dowry demand if the testimony is believed
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of the victim's father about the 16.02.2001 phone call; testimony of the elder sister about the victim's visit and the previous-night beating; PCO operator's evidence that the victim was weeping; PCO witness seeing the victim weeping; post-mortem opinion on time of death
witness_credibility: Trial court had the demeanour advantage and its view was affirmed; the Supreme Court would not reappraise credibility; the testimony was accepted 'if he is to be believed (In fact, two courts have)'
trial_duration: offence: 16.02.2001/17.02.2001 (death); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 27.02.2015; Supreme Court: 26.09.2018
legal_representation: Appellant: Dr. J.P. Dhanda, Ms. Raj Rani Dhanda, Vineet Dhanda, N.A. Usmani, K.P. Singh, Gopi Chand (Advs.); State: Ms. Jaspreet Gogia, Ms. Manadakini Singh (Advs.)
investigation_status: FIR lodged 17.02.2001; post-mortem conducted 28.02.2001; charge sheet not stated; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.304-B, 8 years RI. High Court: conviction affirmed, sentence reduced to 7 years RI. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Neighbour witnesses (defence DW6 and DW8) should not be relied on; the evidence of PW1 and PW3 shows proximity in time between the alleged acts and the death
defence_argument: No cruelty or dowry demand established; the victim's death was attributed to taunts by her sister (PW3); the appellant financed the victim's education and the father-in-law financed her education
legal_principle_applied: Limited scope of interference under Art.136 in concurrent findings; s.113-B presumption is rebuttable and triggered where cruelty for dowry is shown soon before death; 'soon before' is a relative expression
precedent_relied_upon: Relied on: Saravanabhavan and Govindaswamy v. State of Madras AIR 1966 SC 1273; Mst. Dalbir Kaur and Others v. State of Punjab (1976) 4 SCC 158. Referred to: Sushil Ansal (2014) 6 SCC 173; Major Singh (2015) 5 SCC 201; Rajinder Singh (2015) 6 SCC 477; G.V. Siddaramesh (2010) 3 SCC 152; Ashok Kumar (2010) 12 SCC 350; Mohd. Ali alias Guddu (2015) 7 SCC 272; Ganga Kumar Srivastava (2005) 6 SCC 211
judicial_aggravating_factors: Alleged cruelty proximate in time to the death (previous-night beating), if believed
